title: The Sow and Her Piglets
intro_lines: Grunts echo from the brush.
A sow roots beside her striped piglets.

outcomes.text: You slip back through the brush as the sounder moves on.
A piglet squeals and the sow gores your thigh before you flee.
Sparks scatter the sounder; you pocket a broken tusk.
The sow lowers her head and rips your calf open.
They gorge while you slip past, unnoticed.
They finish eating and follow, demanding more.
The scent draws a second boar from the thicket.

history_note: Feral pigs were put ashore by sailors as living larders and charge with tusks when cornered with young.

title: The Night Thieves
intro_lines: Something clicks outside the tent flap.
Your belt buckle is gone.

outcomes.text: You trace clicks to a burrow: your buckle and a pearl.
A claw the size of your fist clamps your ankle.
The burrow is empty; the thief has moved on.
It takes the bait and is caught; your gear is safe.
It drags the trap into the surf, bait and all.

choices.label: Throw stones to drive them off

outcomes.text: The crabs retreat into the rocks, clicking.
One pins your hand under a rock before fleeing.

history_note: Coconut crabs climb palms, strike with claws of roughly 3,300 newtons, and steal shiny objects.

title: The Emerald Coil
intro_lines: Something heavy hangs above the trail.
Yellow eyes blink from the leaves.

outcomes.text: The boa drops dead and you skin it for supper.
The wounded boa falls on you and coils tight.
You pass beneath the coil without waking it.
A branch snaps and the boa strikes at your face.
Smoke drives the boa into the canopy above.
Fire spreads through the ferns; you retreat singed.

history_note: Tree boas ambush prey from branches, and moray eels bite hands poked into reef crevices.

title: The Troop at the Gate
intro_lines: Screeching fills the camp.
Macaques tear through your stores.

choices.label: Beat drums and drive them off

outcomes.text: The troop flees with only a sack of copra.
The alpha charges and you take scratches before they break.
They gorge on scraps and retreat into the trees.
They tear your tent apart for the good stores.
Tide-Puck hisses and the troop scatters into the jungle.
The troop turns on Tide-Puck; you drag him away bleeding.

history_note: Macaques raid camps for food and shiny tools, and their alarm calls warn of predators.

title: Blood in the Shallows
intro_lines: Your cut drips into the tide pool.
A grey shape circles once, twice.

outcomes.text: The reef shark loses interest and slips away into deeper water.
It bumps your leg; you kick free with a bruised shin but keep your footing.
Teeth rake your calf. Tide-Puck drags you up the beach, bleeding.

choices.label: Hurl a fish to distract it

outcomes.text: The shark takes the fish and vanishes; you limp to shore.
It ignores the fish and circles closer; you back away slowly.
Two more sharks appear, drawn by the thrashing fish.

history_note: Reef sharks are drawn by blood and thrashing in shallow water, a documented hazard for waders and fishers.

title: Tiger at Dusk
intro_lines: The sun bleeds into the horizon.
A dark fin cuts the glassy water.

outcomes.text: You reach ankle-deep water; the tiger shark turns back to deep blue.
It grazes your paddle; you stumble but gain the shallows.
It strikes the boat; you swim hard for shore, losing gear.
The shark circles, nudges you, then drifts away at last.
It takes a test bite of your pack; you kick free, wounded.
It drags you under briefly; Tide-Puck's barking drives it off.

history_note: Tiger sharks hunt at dusk in shallow coastal water, a well-documented risk to swimmers and small boats.

title: Stingray in the Sand
intro_lines: A dimple in the sand shifts.
Something flat lies buried there.

outcomes.text: The ray lifts and glides away; you pass unharmed.
It startles; a wing brushes your ankle, no sting.
The barb catches your foot; hot water is the only relief.
The stick touches the ray; it bolts and leaves a shallow scrape.
The ray ignores the stick; you retreat and go around.
The stick snaps; the ray stings your hand as you flinch.

history_note: Stingrays bury in sand and injure when stepped on; shuffling feet is the standard avoidance.

title: Moray in the Crevice
intro_lines: Your hand reaches into a dark crack.
Teeth flash in the murk.

outcomes.text: The moray holds its ground; you withdraw with only a scare.
It lunges but misses; your wrist grazes coral, stinging.
Jaws clamp your fingers; Tide-Puck yanks your arm free, bleeding.
The moray retreats deep; you pry loose a cache of shells.
It bites the spear shaft; you keep the head but lose the shaft.
It strikes past the spear and tears your palm before bolting.

history_note: Moray eels bite when hands enter crevices and may carry ciguatera toxin.

title: Stonefish on the Reef
intro_lines: A lump of rock that breathes.
You almost step on it.

outcomes.text: You freeze in time; the stonefish never moves. You retreat.
Your boot slips; you skin your knee but avoid the spines.
A spine pierces your sole; hot water and a long, sick night.
Tide-Puck growls and circles the spot; you step wide.
Tide-Puck sniffs too close and yelps; you carry him to camp.
He startles the fish; it bolts and you lose the trail.

history_note: Stonefish venom spines cause severe pain and require hot-water immersion; they camouflage as rock.

title: Turtles at Moonrise
intro_lines: Moonlight on the sand.
A turtle hauls herself up.

outcomes.text: She lays her eggs and returns to sea; you mark the nest.
She aborts and slides back; the nest site is lost.
A second turtle mistakes you for a predator and charges.

choices.label: Flip her for meat and shell

outcomes.text: You secure meat and a shell vessel; the nest is ruined.
She rights herself and bites your hand before escaping.
Two more turtles arrive; you herd them into a pen.

history_note: Sea turtles nest at night and were historically flipped onto their backs to capture.

title: Frigatebird Shadow
intro_lines: A black bird hangs motionless.
It drops a fish at your feet.

outcomes.text: The frigatebird shrieks and dives; you gain a free meal.
It snatches the fish back and steals a shiny trinket.
More frigatebirds arrive, harassing you for scraps.

choices.label: Throw a stone to drive it off

outcomes.text: It wheels away; you keep your peace and your things.
The stone misses; the bird circles but does not land.
You hit a companion bird; the flock mobs you briefly.

history_note: Frigatebirds steal fish and shiny objects, a known nuisance to sailors and castaways.

title: Tern Colony Eggs
intro_lines: Thousands of terns wheel overhead.
Eggs lie in shallow scrapes.

outcomes.text: You fill a sack with eggs; the colony screams but holds.
Terns dive and peck; you retreat with a few eggs.
You slip on guano; eggs break and birds swarm.
Two terns caught; you smoke the meat for travel.
Snares tangle; you free one bird and lose the rope.
Colony abandons the site; nothing gained but guilt.

history_note: Tern colonies provided eggs and meat to castaways such as those on Tromelin Island.

title: Fever Mosquitoes
intro_lines: Dusk brings a whining cloud.
Your skin prickles and burns.

outcomes.text: Smoke drives them off; you sleep soundly at last.
Smoke stings your eyes; fewer bites but a restless night.
Fire catches a palm; you beat it out, exhausted.
Herbs soothe the bites; no fever takes hold.
Bites swell; you shiver through a mild fever by morning.
Fever spikes; you sweat through two days in the shade.

history_note: Mosquitoes spread fever among camped sailors, a common killer on tropical havens.

title: Parrot That Talks
intro_lines: A green parrot watches you.
It repeats your own words.

outcomes.text: It learns to call out 'sail!' on cue; a handy lookout.
It learns nothing useful but squawks all night.
It flies off, carrying a shiny button from your coat.
You net it; a haven buyer will pay well for a talker.
It bites your finger and escapes, squawking insults.
The flock descends; you flee, losing the net.

history_note: Parrots mimicked speech and were sold in pirate havens as prized curiosities.

title: Crab That Steals
intro_lines: Something clicks in the dark.
Your knife is gone.

outcomes.text: You find the burrow and recover the knife plus a pearl.
The burrow is empty; the trail vanishes in sand.
You stumble into a second crab; it pinches hard.
The crab emerges; you reclaim your knife and more.
A larger crab takes the bait and the knife both.
Nothing comes; ants eat the fish by morning.

history_note: Coconut crabs scavenge and steal shiny objects, with claws strong enough to crush.

title: Cliff-Goat Snare
intro_lines: Tide-Puck stiffens, nose aimed at the basalt ledges above.
Feral goats graze the sparse grass — descendants

choices.label: Set wire nooses on game trails

outcomes.text: A yearling nanny catches her leg; you dispatch it cleanly. Meat and hide for camp.
The billy charges the snare line, horns slashing your forearm before breaking free.
A UTC patrol spots the snares from the ridge. They confiscate gear and fine you.

choices.label: Drive goats toward a box canyon

outcomes.text: Puck herds three kids into the dead-end. Easy capture — milk and meat for weeks.
The nannies panic, scatter over the cliff edge. Only one carcass recoverable.
Loose rock gives way under Puck. He falls twenty feet — bruised but breathing.

choices.label: Observe from cover, learn their water

outcomes.text: You find a seep behind a lava tube — fresh water and a natural trap site for future.
Rain closes in before you locate it. Wet, cold, and empty-handed.

history_note: Alexander Selkirk tamed feral goats on Juan Fernández for milk and company, running them down on foot and building huts from their skins.

title: Boar Pit at the Wallow
intro_lines: Churned mud and tusk-gouged trees mark a sounder's daily
The big boar's spoor is fresh — he'll return at dusk.

choices.label: Dig a deep pit, stake it

outcomes.text: The boar drops at twilight. Six hundred pounds of meat, tusks for tools.
A sow falls in instead, squealing. The boar circles, charging the edge — you barely climb clear.
Rain collapses the pit walls overnight. Wasted labour, wasted stakes.

choices.label: Lure with fermented coconut mash, shoot

outcomes.text: The mash works. One ball drops the boar clean. Meat smokes by midnight.
Shot goes low. Wounded boar vanishes into mangroves — blood trail lost in tide.
Monkeys raid the mash, get drunk, and mob your stand. You retreat empty-handed.

choices.label: Leave it be — boar root up crab beds

outcomes.text: You mark the wallow. Later, a UTC patrol blunders into the sounder — chaos buys you intel.
The boar finds your outpost midden instead. Fence splintered, stores scattered.

history_note: Sailors introduced feral pigs as living larders; they root up ground, eat crab juveniles, and charge with tusks causing deep leg wounds when cornered.

title: Bird-Lime on the Tern Colony
intro_lines: Sooty terns carpet the cay — tens of thousands screaming
Tromelin castaways lived on them for fifteen years. You can

choices.label: Smear lime on low branches, wait

outcomes.text: Dozens stick fast. You club and pluck until your arms ache. Eggs too.
A frigatebird dives through the lime, tangles, crashes — colony erupts. Cloud of beaks and claws.
Heat melts the lime. Birds avoid it. Wasted shells, wasted dawn.

choices.label: Build a hide, net fledglings at night

outcomes.text: Puck flushes chicks into the net silently. Adults never wake. Clean harvest.
A rat snake drops from above onto Puck. He kills it, but the strike draws blood.
Tideborn scouts observe from the reef. They leave a shell offering — neutral contact.

choices.label: Take only eggs — sustainable, less noise

outcomes.text: Basket full before sunrise. Rich protein, colony undisturbed for next season.
A tern pecks your hand deep. Infection risk — herbs needed fast.

history_note: Tromelin castaways survived fifteen years eating sooty terns from colonies of tens of thousands, keeping one fire alive with wreck timber and driftwood.

title: Stone Fish Weir at Ebb
intro_lines: The tide pulls back, exposing the reef flat. Jacks
A wall of coral rubble now could funnel them into a holding

choices.label: Build a V-weir with the outgoing current

outcomes.text: The weir fills each ebb. Steady fish, no powder, no hooks lost.
A moray claims the pen. Bitten hand hauling the catch — hot water helps, but fever follows.
Storm surge smashes the wall. Rebuild needed, stones scattered.

choices.label: Spear the pools by torchlight with Puck

outcomes.text: Puck's eyes catch the flash of scales. You spear eight fat jacks in an hour.
Stonefish camouflage works. Spike through boot — agony, swelling, night of sweats.
Torch draws a UTC cutter's attention. They board, seize half the catch.

choices.label: Poison the pool with crushed derris

outcomes.text: Fish float belly-up. Easy gathering, but the meat tastes metallic. Ciguatera risk.
Current shifts. Poison kills the coral, drives off fish for weeks. Waste.
Tideborn scout confronts you. Reef is sacred. They take your knife as forfeit.

history_note: Tromelin castaways caught reef fish — jacks, groupers, triggerfish — by line, spear, and tide-pool gathering on the exposed reef flat.

title: Coconut Crab Trap Line
intro_lines: Moonlight glints on armoured claws the size of your fist.
Coconut crabs climb palms, steal shiny things, taste like

choices.label: Bait coconut halves on weighted lines

outcomes.text: Five monsters in the buckets. Meat for days, claws for hooks, one wore a gold ring.
Biggest male crushes the bucket, climbs the line, nips your finger to bone.
Hermit crabs swarm the bait. Nothing worth keeping but the shells.

choices.label: Dig pit traps under palm trunks, funnel

outcomes.text: Crabs fall in climbing down at dawn. Easy capture, no injured fingers.
A wild boar smashes the pits rooting for grubs. Traps ruined, boar gets fat.
Tide-Puck investigates a pit, falls in. Claws click on his shell — he's stuck.

choices.label: Trade with free pirates — they know

outcomes.text: Quartermaster shares a hidden grove. You return with a sack of giants.
Pirates water the rum. You wake robbed, crab-less, with a headache.

history_note: Coconut crabs (Birgus latro) climb palms, exert claw forces up to 3,300 newtons, scavenge shiny objects, and are prized for meat but overharvested.

title: Rats in the Stores
intro_lines: Gnawed sacks, scattered grain, droppings like black rice.
They came on the wreck — ship rats, bold and multiplying.

outcomes.text: Twenty dead by morning. Stores secure. Tide-Puck presents you with the largest.
A trap snaps on your finger checking it. Broken nail, blood, curses.
Rats avoid the traps. They've learned. Infestation grows.

choices.label: Train Tide-Puck as a ratter — instinct

outcomes.text: Puck becomes a terror. He brings you trophies daily. The holds stay clean.
He corners a nest in the cave. Mother rat bites his nose — nasty gash.
He eats his catches. Grows fat, lazy, ignores commands for a week.

choices.label: Seal the stores with tar and sailcloth

outcomes.text: Airtight drums. Rats vanish within a week. Stores safe for months.
They chew through the cloth before the tar sets. Wasted supplies.
Condensation inside the drums moulds the grain. Total loss.

history_note: Alexander Selkirk's feet were gnawed by rats at night on Juan Fernández; he tamed feral cats to control them and read the Bible aloud to keep his speech.

title: Wreck-Hounds on the Wind
intro_lines: Low throats bay in the mist — not wolves, but dogs gone
They know the island. They know you. And they're hungry.

choices.label: Stand ground, fire a volley, drive them

outcomes.text: Smoke and thunder scatter the pack. One drops — collar bears a UTC brand.
The alpha charges through the smoke. Jaws on your thigh before Puck distracts it.
Shots miss. Pack circles, waits. You retreat to the outpost, besieged till dawn.

choices.label: Throw meat, back away — buy peace

outcomes.text: They eat, sniff the air, trot off. The alpha pauses, looks back — truce held.
Meat only whets them. They take the food and flank you. Puck growls, hair up.
A Tideborn scout whistles — the pack obeys. Dogs were theirs. They nod at you.

choices.label: Follow at dawn — find their den, maybe

outcomes.text: Cave den found. Three pups, eyes open. Mother watches but doesn't attack. You take one.
Den empty — they moved. Tracks lead to a UTC camp. Dogs were their sentries.
Mother ambushes from above. Puck fights her off, but both bleed badly.

history_note: Dogs from wrecked ships often survive on islands; Pedro Serrano encountered a second castaway after years alone, and conflict with other survivors was a documented risk.

title: Jungle Fowl at Dust-Bath
intro_lines: Feathers dust the dry earth — red jungle fowl, ancestors
They scratch, bathe, crow. Unaware the noose waits.

outcomes.text: Two cocks, three hens in the bag. Meat, eggs, feathers for arrows.
A monitor lizard triggers a noose. It thrashes, cuts the line, escapes.
Monkeys watch, copy your knots. Next dawn your snares are gone, fibre in trees.
Clean kills. Best hen for breeding, cock for the pot. No alarm raised.
Dart misses, hits a parrot. It screams, flock erupts. Fowl vanish.
You nick your own thumb loading. Numbness spreads. Hour of panic.

choices.label: Leave grain trail to a pen —

outcomes.text: They come daily. Hens lay in your nest boxes. Sustainable protein.
Rats eat the grain. Fowl ignore it. Pen stands empty.
A feral cat takes up residence in the pen. Hens stop coming.

history_note: Sailors left chickens on islands as living larders; feral jungle fowl revert to wild type quickly, dust-bathing and roosting in predictable patterns trappers exploit.

title: The Cave at Creek's End
intro_lines: The cave smells of brine, copper, and something floral —
Walls glitter with embedded shell. A pool reflects

outcomes.text: You push through the water-curtain. A dry chamber. Tideborn glyphs cover the walls. In the centre, a nest of woven seaweed cradles an egg — pulsing, bioluminescent.
The water surges. A shape lunges — not the Sovereign, but a guardian: eel-headed, crab-clawed. Puck intercepts. You flee, glyphs unread.
Charcoal rubbings made. The glyphs depict a binding ritual — chains, crystals, the Sovereign thrashing. UTC dark-binding crystals match the drawings.
The pool boils as you work. You flee, rubbings incomplete. The glyphs fade behind you.
You snatch it. The cave shrieks — not sound, but pressure in your skull. Puck howls. You run, the egg cold and heavy in your arms.
Your fingers close on shell — then a hand closes on your wrist. Tideborn. Pale, gilled, silent. They take the egg. You leave empty-handed but alive.

history_note: Pedro Serrano on Serrana Bank used shells as rain catchers holding up to 12 gallons, dove for two stones to strike sparks, and built a fire hut from seaweed and wreck planks.

title: Consequences at the Fire
intro_lines: Night falls. The camp fire cracks. Whatever happened
Silas watches. Puck sleeps — or feigns it. The egg

choices.label: If you have the egg: hatch it, bind it

outcomes.text: The egg hatches into a Mythos — not Sovereign, but kin. It imprints on Puck. UTC crystals glow red in its presence.
It hatches wrong. Twisted, ravenous. It eats your stores, then turns on Puck. You put it down. The guilt stays.
A UTC warship appears at dawn. Their crystals track the egg. They shell the beach. You flee inland.

choices.label: If you have the glyphs: share

outcomes.text: Silas knows a retired UTC boatswain turned pirate. He confirms the crystal weakness. A raid is planned.
The boatswain betrays you. UTC ambush at the rendezvous. Silas takes a ball to the shoulder. You drag him back.

choices.label: If you have neither: the Tideborn

outcomes.text: A scout waits at the fire. The egg in a kelp basket. 'The Sovereign wakes. The binding breaks. You will help us — or we all drown.'
No one comes. But at dawn, the UTC camp is gone — burned, crystals shattered. Tideborn arrows in the sand. A warning delivered.

history_note: Ada Blackjack on Wrangel Island nursed a dying man through scurvy, barricaded his body against animals, taught herself to shoot and trap, and survived alone with her cat Vic until rescue.
